items.stickyText: Create a more techish looking site rather than Lucid default style. Use basic styling from "Desig Loop" for fonts and color scheme on the site. INclude the background shader animation used on Design Loop also.
items.author: John Dilworth
items.interpretation: Restyle the whole site with a more technical look instead of the Lucid default style: Design Loop's fonts and colour scheme, plus Design Loop's animated ASCII background behind the hero.
items.proposedChange: Swap the site's type and colour tokens in styles.css for Design Loop's (fonts, accent colours, surfaces), and port Design Loop's AsciiBackground canvas animation to a small inline vanilla-JS canvas behind the hero (no external scripts; static frame for reduced motion and during capture). Done together with item 3, since Design Loop's palette is dark.

items.stickyText: Revert headline back to "Turn every sticky note into a pull request"
items.author: John Dilworth
items.interpretation: Change the hero headline from "Every sticky note becomes a change" back to the cycle 2 wording.
items.proposedChange: Set the hero h1 to "Turn every sticky note into a pull request" (and the page title/meta description to match if they use the current headline).

items.stickyText: Add darkmode to the site — and make dark the default.
items.author: John Dilworth
items.interpretation: Add a dark mode and make dark the default.
items.proposedChange: Add a dark theme as the default with a sun/moon toggle in the header that remembers the choice (localStorage, no external code); recolour the section bands (orange, teal, grey) and SVG icon strokes for dark. Pairs with item 1.

items.stickyText:
Add a section to explain the approval flow that allows collaboration, but also keeps changes in approval flow by specific people - highlight the different modes:

Auto - run on autopilot, incorporating changes on a regular schedule automatically. 

Manual - run a harvest at your own schedule

---

Approver mode — let's an assigned individual manually approve and adjust each change before it is incorporated into code.
items.author: John Dilworth
items.interpretation: Add a section explaining Harvest's approval flow: anyone can collaborate, but named people control what gets built. Highlight three modes: Auto (runs on a schedule automatically), Manual (run a harvest whenever you want) and Approver (an assigned person approves or edits each change before it goes into code).
items.proposedChange: Add a new "You choose who approves" section after the Review/Harvest/Ship/Repeat loop with three cards: Auto, Manual and Approver mode, using the sticky's descriptions (copy tidied), plus a nav link if it fits.

items.stickyText: Make each of these icons an "X"    or cancel emoji so it's clear these are problems that exist with  current software.
items.author: John Dilworth
items.interpretation: In the problem section, replace the three card icons with an X or cancel mark so they read as problems with today's tools.
items.proposedChange: Replace the three problem-card SVG icons with a matching red X-in-circle icon (inline SVG, not emoji, so it renders the same everywhere).

items.stickyText: Update the site with screenshots from "harvest dashboard" project
items.author: John Dilworth
items.interpretation: Use real screenshots of the Harvest Dashboard project on the site.
items.proposedChange: Capture current Harvest Dashboard pages (home cards, single-page project view, approval list) at harvest-dashboard.netlify.app, add them as compressed .webp images (each well under 2 MB) and use them in the 'Works with your agents' area and the evolution/proof section in place of the older Design Loop shots where they fit. Which spots to replace is a judgement call; say so if you want them somewhere specific.
